name: Design secure access to AWS resources

lesson.summary: Secure access means giving the right identities only the permissions they need. Use IAM roles and temporary credentials instead of long-lived keys, centralize workforce access with IAM Identity Center, use Cognito for application customers, and apply guardrails with SCPs and permissions boundaries across accounts.
keyPoints: Use roles and temporary credentials via STS, not long-lived access keys
IAM policy evaluation: explicit deny wins, then SCPs and boundaries cap permissions, and an allow must still exist
Cross-account access needs trust or resource policy in the owner and an allow in the caller
SCPs never grant permissions; they limit what accounts can do
Cognito user pools authenticate customers; identity pools issue AWS credentials
IAM Identity Center provides workforce SSO across accounts

scenarios.text: A company is building a mobile photo app for millions of consumers. Users sign in with their Google or Facebook accounts and upload photos straight to an Amazon S3 bucket. The security team forbids embedding long-lived AWS credentials in the app.

A company runs an on-premises Active Directory and has 40 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. Employees must sign in once with their corporate credentials and reach only the AWS accounts and permission levels assigned to their job role. The security team wants no individual IAM users and as little ongoing administration as possible.

questions.prompt: An application on Amazon EC2 must read objects from an S3 bucket. Which approach follows AWS security best practice?

options.text: Store an IAM user's access key in the application configuration file
Embed the access key in the AMI so it is always available
Attach an IAM role to the instance through an instance profile
Make the bucket public so no credentials are needed

questions.explanation: An instance profile role gives the application automatically rotated temporary credentials with no secrets to manage. A stored access key is a long-lived credential that can leak. Baking a key into the AMI spreads it to every copy of the image. A public bucket exposes the data to everyone.

questions.prompt: A company wants to guarantee that no principal in any member account, including account administrators, can launch resources outside two approved Regions. What should the solution architect use?

options.text: An IAM permissions boundary attached to every administrator
A network ACL on each VPC
An IAM group policy in the management account
A service control policy attached to the organizational unit

questions.explanation: An SCP sets the maximum permissions for all principals in the affected accounts, so a Region-deny SCP cannot be overridden by account admins. Permissions boundaries apply per user or role and must be managed in each account. Network ACLs filter subnet traffic, not API calls. IAM groups in the management account do not affect member accounts.

questions.prompt: A platform team lets developers create their own IAM roles for Lambda functions. The team must make sure developers cannot create a role with more permissions than a defined maximum. Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Give developers the iam:CreateRole permission only and review roles monthly
Require that developers attach a permissions boundary when creating roles, using a condition in their IAM policy
Enable MFA for all developers
Use an SCP that denies all IAM actions

questions.explanation: Delegating role creation with a condition that forces a permissions boundary caps the effective permissions of any role the developers create. Monthly review is detective, not preventive. MFA verifies identity but does not limit permissions. Denying all IAM actions would stop developers from creating roles at all.

questions.prompt: A role in account A must read objects in an S3 bucket owned by account B. The bucket policy in account B allows the role's ARN. The role still gets Access Denied. What is the most likely missing piece?

options.text: The role in account A has no identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject on the bucket
The bucket in account B needs versioning enabled
Account B must create an IAM user for the role
S3 does not support cross-account access

questions.explanation: For cross-account access to a resource, both the resource policy in the owning account and an identity policy in the requesting account must allow the action. Versioning is unrelated to authorization. Creating a user is unnecessary because the role already authenticates in account A. S3 does support cross-account access.

questions.prompt: Which TWO actions align with IAM best practices for securing access? (Choose two.)

options.text: Require multi-factor authentication for human users
Share the root user password with the operations team for emergencies
Create long-lived access keys for each application
Use IAM roles with temporary credentials for workloads
Attach AdministratorAccess to all developers to avoid blocked work

questions.explanation: MFA protects human identities and roles supply short-lived credentials to workloads. Sharing the root password removes accountability. Long-lived keys are a leak risk. Giving everyone administrator access violates least privilege.

questions.statement: A service control policy that allows an action grants that permission to the IAM users and roles in the member accounts.
questions.explanation: False. An SCP only sets a permission guardrail; principals still need an identity-based or resource-based policy that grants the action.

questions.prompt: Put these steps in order for a user in account A to access resources in account B using a role.
steps: The user calls sts:AssumeRole and receives temporary credentials
An administrator in account B creates a role whose trust policy names account A
An administrator in account A allows the user to call sts:AssumeRole on that role ARN
An administrator in account B attaches permissions to the role
questions.explanation: The role and its trust policy come first, then its permissions, then the account A user is allowed to assume it, and only then can the user call AssumeRole to get temporary credentials.

questions.prompt: Which Cognito component should the company use to handle sign-up, sign-in, and Google or Facebook federation for the app's users?

options.text: Cognito identity pool
Cognito user pool
IAM Identity Center
AWS Directory Service

questions.explanation: A user pool is the user directory that handles sign-up, sign-in, and social federation and issues tokens. An identity pool exchanges identities for AWS credentials rather than providing the directory. IAM Identity Center is for workforce access. Directory Service provides managed Active Directory, not a customer sign-in service.

questions.prompt: How can the mobile app upload directly to S3 without any long-lived AWS keys inside the app?

options.text: Exchange the user's token with a Cognito identity pool for temporary credentials of an IAM role
Ship one shared IAM user access key in the app and rotate it each release
Make the S3 bucket writable by anonymous users
Have each user create an IAM user in the account

questions.explanation: A Cognito identity pool exchanges the authenticated token for short-lived credentials of a scoped IAM role. A shared key in the app can be extracted. Anonymous write access exposes the bucket. Creating IAM users for millions of customers does not scale.

questions.prompt: Match each service to its primary purpose.

pairs.right: Single sign-on for the workforce across AWS accounts
Sign-up and sign-in for an application's customers
Finds resources shared outside the account or organization

questions.explanation: Each pairing reflects the service's documented purpose: workforce SSO, customer identity, guardrails, and external access findings.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function needs a database password that must be rotated automatically every 30 days with the least operational effort. Where should the password be stored?

options.text: An encrypted environment variable on the function
A plaintext file packaged with the function
An S3 object encrypted with SSE-S3
AWS Secrets Manager with managed rotation enabled

questions.explanation: Secrets Manager stores secrets and can rotate supported database credentials on a schedule. Environment variables have no rotation. A packaged plaintext file exposes the secret in the deployment artifact. An S3 object has no rotation feature and needs custom code.

questions.prompt: An EC2 instance in account A must call an API in account B. Which approach avoids storing long-lived keys?

options.text: Create an IAM user in account B and store its key on the instance
Attach an instance profile whose role is allowed to assume a role in account B
Make the account B resources public
Copy the root access keys of account B to the instance

questions.explanation: The instance role gets temporary credentials and can assume a role in account B whose trust policy allows it. Stored IAM user keys are long-lived. Public resources remove access control. Root keys are the most dangerous credential and should not be used.

questions.prompt: An SCP attached to an OU denies all actions outside eu-west-1. A security team needs one break-glass administrator role in each account to be exempt. What is the simplest way?

options.text: Add a condition on the deny that excludes the role ARN using aws:PrincipalArn
Remove the SCP from the OU permanently
Attach an IAM policy to the role that allows all Regions, which overrides the SCP
Move the role into the management account

questions.explanation: SCP deny statements can use condition keys such as aws:PrincipalArn to exempt specific roles. Removing the SCP drops the guardrail for everyone. An IAM allow cannot override an SCP deny. Roles cannot be moved between accounts, and the management account is not affected by SCPs anyway.

questions.prompt: A company wants to be alerted when an S3 bucket policy or IAM role trust policy grants access to a principal outside the organization. Which service provides this?

options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor cost checks
Amazon Inspector
AWS Config managed rule for tagging
IAM Access Analyzer with the organization as the zone of trust

questions.explanation: Access Analyzer produces findings for resources shared outside the chosen zone of trust. Trusted Advisor cost checks look at spending. Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities. A tagging rule checks tags, not sharing.

questions.prompt: A company needs to control who can use an encryption key, audit every use, and disable the key when needed, for data stored in S3. Which choice meets this?

options.text: SSE-S3 with keys managed entirely by S3
Client-side base64 encoding of objects
SSE-KMS with a customer managed key
Making the bucket private only

questions.explanation: A customer managed KMS key has its own key policy, logs each use in CloudTrail, and can be disabled. SSE-S3 keys are not controllable by the customer. Base64 is encoding, not encryption. A private bucket controls access but does not provide key control or auditing.

questions.prompt: Which statement about IAM policy evaluation is correct?

options.text: An explicit allow overrides an explicit deny
Permissions are allowed by default until denied
The order of statements in the policy decides the result
An explicit deny overrides any allow

questions.explanation: An explicit deny always wins over an allow. The default is an implicit deny, so an allow is required. Statement order has no effect on the result.

questions.prompt: A central networking account owns subnets that several other accounts in the organization must launch EC2 instances into, without duplicating the VPC. What should be used?

options.text: VPC peering from every account to every other account
Share the subnets with AWS Resource Access Manager
Copy the VPC with a CloudFormation template to each account
Create IAM users in the networking account for each team

questions.explanation: RAM VPC sharing lets participant accounts launch resources into subnets owned by another account in the organization. Peering connects separate VPCs rather than sharing one. Copying duplicates the network. IAM users do not make subnets available to other accounts.

questions.prompt: Which TWO measures help ensure engineers use temporary credentials rather than long-lived access keys? (Choose two.)

options.text: Federate workforce sign-in through IAM Identity Center
Share one IAM user access key per team in a wiki
Use IAM roles for workloads running on AWS compute
Create access keys for the root user
Disable MFA to simplify sign-in

questions.explanation: Identity Center provides temporary credentials for people, and roles provide them for workloads. A shared key is long-lived and untraceable. Root access keys are a high-risk long-lived credential. Disabling MFA weakens security without addressing credentials.

questions.prompt: A company wants to stop member accounts from disabling CloudTrail and from leaving the organization. Which TWO statements describe a correct design? (Choose two.)

options.text: Attach an SCP that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail
Add an IAM policy in each account that denies the same actions, since SCPs cannot deny
Attach an SCP that denies organizations:LeaveOrganization
Apply the SCP to the management account to protect the members
Rely on tags to block the actions

questions.explanation: SCPs can explicitly deny those API actions for all principals in the member accounts. Per-account IAM policies can be changed by account administrators, so they are not a guardrail. SCPs do not restrict the management account and do not protect members through it. Tags do not block API calls on their own.

questions.prompt: Which solution meets the requirements with the least operational overhead?

options.text: Create IAM users in each of the 40 accounts and sync passwords with a script
Enable IAM Identity Center, connect it to the Active Directory, and assign permission sets to groups for each account
Build a custom SAML broker on EC2 and a role in each account
Share one administrator role across all accounts with a single password

questions.explanation: Identity Center integrates with Active Directory and assigns permission sets to groups across accounts centrally with temporary credentials. Per-account IAM users violate the requirement and add work. A custom broker needs ongoing maintenance. A shared password gives no role-based least privilege.

questions.prompt: Put these steps in order to restrict a test OU so its accounts can use only approved services.
steps: Verify access in a sandbox account in the OU
Create an SCP that allows only the approved services
Detach the default FullAWSAccess SCP from the OU
Attach the new SCP to the OU
questions.explanation: The SCP must exist before it can be attached. Attaching the allow-list SCP first and then detaching the default FullAWSAccess SCP avoids a window with no permissions, and verification comes last.
